newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU farm budget underspent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: EU farm budget underspent in 1996.

text.p: The European Union's farm budget was underspent last year despite the cost of the mad cow crisis which was funded without drawing on the special 198-million-Ecu BSE (bovine spongiform encephalopathy) reserve fund, the European Commission said on Tuesday.

In its latest early warning system report for the 1996 financial year which ended on October 15, the Commission put the amount left unspent in the EAGGF (agricultural guidance and guarantee fund) at 1.758 billion Ecus.
Total expenditure for the EU's common agricultural policy was 39.070 billion Ecus from a total budget of 40.828 billion.

Eradication of BSE in the United Kingdom cost the budget 230 million Ecus in 1996 including the 194-million-Ecu cost of the 70 percent part-financing of buying some 480,000 cattle over 30 months old from producers in the UK, 63,000 in the Netherlands and 72,000 ex-UK animals in France.

The cost of carcass disposal in the UK was lower than expected due to delays in getting the incineration programme started. By October 15, 647,000 animals had been slaughtered, 553,000 rendered but only 25,000 incinerated.
The entire EU contribution is paid only once carcasses have been destroyed but the Commission decided to pay an 80 percent advance after rendering, costing 125 million Ecus.
The cost of the UK's intended selective slaughter programme involving an estimated 150,000 animals, together with a cull of 2,000 animals in Portugal will be carried into the 1997 budget.
This is put at 101 million Ecus for the UK and one million Ecus for Portugal.
Under-expenditure from the 1996 budget included arable crops, sugar, dairy and sheepmeat sectors.

The main fall in the arables sector was 130 million Ecus due to reduced advances of oilseed aid. A further 200 million was saved on the cost of aid for durum wheat not paid in Italy for the 1994 and 1995 marketing years because of increased checks.

Sugar exports were down by 15,000 tonnes because traders concentrated on non-quota C sugar sales on the world market leading to a fall in expected expenditure on export refunds of around 122 million Ecus.
There was an increase in expenditure in the fruit and vegetable sector becuase of higher than expected export refunds by around 15 million Ecus.
The rural development sector cost an extra 35 million Ecus due to increrased payments for suckler cow premia in mixed herds.
Currency fluctuations led to an overspend of 17 million Ecus in the part financing of aid for agri-monetary changes, the so-called green rate used to calculate EU CAP payments.
